name: Chinese skullcap (Scutellaria baicalensis)
short: Liver injury: case reports; 72 confirmed cases in 75,564 (0.095%) in Chinese hospitals, more at high daily amounts; 4 of 37 (10.8%) on formulas with it. 17 users: no significant liver test change.
text: Liver injury has been reported with Chinese skullcap in case reports, a multicentre hospital cohort and a clinic survey. A 2019 letter with no abstract is titled as reporting drug-induced liver injury secondary to Scutellaria baicalensis, and a 2025 case report describes a 50-year-old woman hospitalised with liver injury attributed to a herbal decoction containing Scutellaria root, after a prior similar episode, whose liver tests returned to normal after she stopped it and received liver-protective treatment (the abstract does not say whether the decoction contained other herbs). In a retrospective study at four Shanghai hospitals of traditional Chinese medicine, the confirmed incidence of liver injury from Scutellaria baicalensis and its preparations was 0.095% (72 of 75,564; the abstract does not define this denominator, out of 1,928,526 outpatients screened), and daily doses above the pharmacopoeia recommendation (more than 10 g a day) significantly increased the risk; the abstract does not say how many patients took the herb on its own, and it reports that a variant of the ABCB1 gene was a genetic risk factor; the abstract's conclusion also mentions 'clinically important valvular problems' without giving any data on them. In a clinic survey of Kampo formulas containing Scutellaria root (combination products whose other ingredients the abstract does not list), 4 of 37 patients (10.8%) developed liver injury and all recovered quickly after stopping. On the other side, in 17 patients who took dried Scutellaria baicalensis root daily for an average of 444 days, liver tests did not change significantly and none had signs of liver dysfunction; those authors noted that in each published case report they reviewed, the patient was also taking at least one other supplement linked to liver problems. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
